applicable_when: The kernel uses 255 registers/thread (hardware maximum on H200), limiting occupancy to 12.5% (2 blocks/SM, 8 warps/SM vs 64 max). This causes 58% no-eligible scheduler cycles. The root cause is BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128 which creates a 128x128=16384-element FP32 accumulator requiring enormous register space. Three prior autotune attempts all produced max_diff ~9.4e+02 — a large, consistent error that is NOT a precision issue but a grid coverage bug: kernel_function hardcodes grid=(256,1,1) which is correct only for BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128 (ceil(256/128)*ceil(16384/128)=2*128=256). When autotune changes tile sizes (e.g., BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64), the grid must be recomputed as ceil(256/64)*ceil(16384/64)=4*256=1024, but the hardcoded grid=256 only covers 1/4 of the output, leaving 3/4 unwritten (zeros), producing the observed large max_diff. The fix is to make the grid a lambda meta: (...) function in kernel_function, computing it from M, N, BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N at launch time. With a correct dynamic grid, reducing to BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64 cuts the accumulator from 16384 to 4096 elements, freeing ~75% of registers and allowing 4-8x more warps per SM.
